approve_latency_ms.note: n=19 steady-state from timed probe; n=2000 run blocked by client-side bottleneck. p95/p99 are meaningful (not just max) with n=19, unlike n=20 where both were the max.

breakdown_ms.note: mcp_post_to_visible = time for MCP POST to be processed, approval created, and visible in bootstrap poll. answer_post = time to POST answer, includes persist_grant with app_state::edit (exclusive flock + JSON load/save + fsync). Neither is a fixed poll interval; the 160ms p50 in Q5 v1 was TLS handshake overhead (new HTTPS connection per poll), a measurement artifact.

capacity.knee: concurrency=1; server collapses with any concurrency (p99 14s at conc=4). Likely cause: persist_grant's app_state::edit takes exclusive flock, serializing all concurrent approvals.
capacity.method: concurrent MCP clients with dedicated phone thread answering
capacity.note: This is a real capacity limit, not measurement artifact. The 10/s in Q5 v1 was the generator's rate, not host capacity.

ci_gate.note: Thresholds provisional until baseline is re-measured on the CI runner. This baseline was measured on a dev VM (2 vCPU, overlay disk), not the CI runner.

method: pooled TLS connections (no handshake overhead), closed-loop MCP approve-write with phone answering via bootstrap poll
